- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.
- If supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 3–8% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model exhibits mean reversion bias — forecast should be closer to 18-day moving average.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to over-predict recovery; reduce forecast by 5–10% if bullish sentiment is low.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or 0.33, model may be under-reacting to events — increase forecast volatility or downward drift by 1–3%.
- When sentiment is bullish but supply net is negative, model often fails to account for policy-induced volatility — add 2–5% downward buffer to forecast.
